hypotheses.reason: Official Stripe CLI sandbox lifetime is 7 days, not approximately 11 minutes.
Single poll loop is approximately 2 GET/s, below documented 25 req/s sandbox global rate; transient 429 remains possible for other reasons.
Could produce a non-transient 4xx when the second async control begins; official testing docs define both methods but failed run did not publish stage-local full trace.
Most wall time is inside async polling; frozen transport converts every urllib HTTPError directly to ProviderHTTPError with no retry.
Stripe documents 429 lock_timeout, including conflicts with internal Stripe background processes, and recommends retry/backoff.
A pure 600-second ceiling miss would raise TimeoutError after a successful GET, but observed error type is ProviderHTTPError.
Failure occurred in provider acquisition/transport before E0 produced a complete calibration result; no evidence of generic-kernel or judgment contradiction.

decision_rule.both_controls_initially_supported: reject H3; classify failure frontier as async polling/transport resilience until contrary evidence
decision_rule.any_nontransient_4xx: retain H3 and inspect exact diagnostic status/body class before any v0.3.6 design
